tagline: A southern bypass beside Clayton, a town growing with highway connections
intro: The Clayton Bypass skirts the southern side of Clayton between Interstate 40 and US 70 Business southeast of town. North Carolina’s Department of Transportation includes it among the state’s scenic byways.
Construction began in 2006, and the bypass was completed in June 2008. Clayton’s population rose from 16,116 in 2010 to 26,307 in 2020.
Traveling westward, begin at the eastern terminus just east of Powhatan, the community halfway between Clayton and Wilson’s Mills. The bypass continues along Clayton’s southern side to Interstate 40.

moments.title: Powhatan
moments.text: Powhatan centers on the junction of Powhatan Road and US 70 Business, halfway between Clayton and Wilson’s Mills. The eastern end of the Clayton Bypass lies just east of this unincorporated community. An athletics complex on Powhatan Road and large chemical and pharmaceutical plants are part of the community.

moments.title: Clayton
moments.text: Clayton lies in western Johnston County, with small portions of the town extending across the county line into Wake County. Clayton’s highway connections help explain its growth: the town had 16,116 residents in 2010 and 26,307 in 2020. Access to I-40 and US 70, together with proximity to the Research Triangle, contributed to that increase. The town belongs to the Neuse River watershed, and its limits extend northeast to the river and beyond. At 111 East Second Street, Town Hall shares its address with The Clayton Center, a performing arts and conference center.

moments.title: Sanders-Hairr House
moments.text: The Sanders-Hairr House near Clayton was built about 1787, well before the bypass. Its two stories and five-bay front combine Georgian and Federal design. Weatherboard covers the frame, while massive, double-shouldered chimneys flank the house at its ends. A one-story porch with a shed roof stretches across the front. The house entered the National Register of Historic Places in 1971.

sources.label: North Carolina Department of Transportation, North Carolina Scenic Byways, fifth edition
